<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflict and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]; [[1 July 2019 Kabul attack]]
**40 people are killed and over 100 injured by a [[car bomb]]ing and [[shooting]] in [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]]. The [[Taliban]] claims responsibility and loses five gunmen. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/07/01/world/asia/afghanistan-bombing-war-museum.html (''New York Times'')]
**Taliban militants overran the Qush Tepa district of [[Jowzjan Province]], resulting in the deaths of over 50 Afghan soldiers. Many others were captured. [https://ariananews.af/taliban-captured-qushtepa-district-killing-dozens/ (ATNNews)]
*[[Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Israel]] strikes multiple [[Iran]]ian and [[Syria]]n military targets outside [[Damascus]] and [[Homs]], killing 16 people and wounding 21. [https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/israel-strikes-iran-hezbollah-targets-in-syria-four-killed-21-wounded-1.7425013 (''Haaretz'')]
**A stray Syrian [[S-200 (missile)|S-200 missile]] fired in response to the Israeli strikes crashes and explodes on a mountain near [[Vouno]] in [[Northern Cyprus]], located 20 km (12 miles) northeast of [[Nicosia]], causing no injuries but starting a fire. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cyprus-crash/unidentified-flying-object-crashes-in-cyprus-no-casualties-minister-idUSKCN1TW15V (Reuters)]
*[[Iranian intervention in Iraq (2014–present)]], [[Iran–Iraq relations]]
**[[Prime Minister of Iraq|Iraqi Prime Minister]] [[Adil Abdul-Mahdi]] signs a decree ordering all [[Iran]]ian-backed [[Shia Islam|Shia]] militias to integrate into the [[Iraqi Armed Forces]] by the end of July. The decree will change the names of the militias such as the [[Popular Mobilization Forces]] to new divisions and brigades within the military. [https://reuters.com/article/uk-usa-iran-iraq/iraq-pm-orders-iran-allied-militias-to-be-reined-in-idUKKCN1TW3EQ (Reuters)] [http://www.rudaw.net/english/middleeast/iraq/01072019 (Rudaw)]
*Nine people were injured in a Houthi drone attack on [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] [[Abha International Airport]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/report-houthi-drone-attack-on-saudi-airport-leaves-nine-injured-1.7428906 (''Haaretz'')]
;Business and economy
*[[Whaling in Japan]]
**[[Japan]] resumes commercial [[whaling]] after 30 years following the country's withdrawal from the [[International Whaling Commission]]. At least 227 whales are expected to be killed through to December. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/jul/01/japan-resumes-commercial-whaling-for-first-time-in-30-years (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Phase-out of lightweight plastic bags]]
**A ban on single-use [[plastic shopping bag]]s comes into force in [[New Zealand]]. Businesses that break the ban will face fines of up to $100,000[[New Zealand dollar|NZD]]. [https://www.gulftoday.ae/news/2019/07/01/new-zealand-bans-single-use-plastic-bags (''Gulf Today'')]
*[[2019 Japan–South Korea trade dispute]]
**Japan announced  tightening of chemical exports to South Korea that are crucial for semiconductor industry. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-southkorea-japan-laborers/japan-to-tighten-export-rules-for-high-tech-materials-to-south-korea-media-idUSKCN1TV089 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*At least 16 people are killed and 45 injured when a bus rolls over on a road in [[Tucumán Province]], Argentina. [https://www.clarin.com/sociedad/10-muertos-tucuman-vuelco-micro-viajaban-jubilados_0_v3kpdzI3o.html (''Clarín'')]
*In [[Lower Saxony]], [[Germany]], a [[Bundeswehr]] helicopter crashes, killing one of the pilots. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-military-helicopter-crashes-near-hanover/a-49430938 (DW)]
*In [[Mexico]], a storm drops over a metre of [[hail]] over parts of [[Guadalajara]], damaging hundreds of houses. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/guadalajara-mexico-hail-1.5196344 (CBC)]

;International relations
*[[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]], [[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**[[Iran]] announces that it has [[enriched uranium|enriched]] more than {{convert|300|kg}} of [[uranium]] to 3.67%, contrary to previous agreement. This is still highly insufficient to produce one nuclear weapon. [https://www.dw.com/en/iran-reported-to-pass-300-kg-limit-on-low-enriched-uranium/a-49428832 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[Japan–United States relations]], [[Japan–North Korea relations]], [[2018–19 Korean peace process]]
**After speaking by phone with [[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]], [[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Japan)|Japanese Foreign Minister]] [[Tarō Kōno]] says "he hopes the meeting adds momentum to efforts toward the denuclearization of the [[Korean Peninsula]]". Kōno also says that [[Prime Minister of Japan|Japanese Prime Minister]] [[Shinzō Abe]] "wants to meet [[Kim Jong-un]] to solve the issue of [[North Korean abductions of Japanese citizens]]". [https://japantoday.com/category/politics/update1-japan-hopes-trump-kim-meeting-spurs-nuclear-abduction-talks (''Japan Today'')]
*[[Libya–Turkey relations]]
**After political pressure from [[Turkey]], six Turkish sailors are released from detention by the [[Libyan National Army]] under general [[Khalifa Haftar]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/jul/01/six-turkish-sailors-freed-by-libya-warlord-khalifa-haftar (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*France's interior minister, [[Christophe Castaner]], has asked the [[Paris]] police chief to provide explanations about a video that went viral on social media, where law enforcement officers are seen spraying with pepper spray and dragging protesters from the ''[[Extinction Rebellion]]'' anti-climate change movement. Although the police needed to evict the protesters, who obstructed a transit route, the mechanisms that they used generated negative reactions. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2019/jul/01/french-police-criticised-over-removal-of-paris-climate-protesters (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Hong Kong anti-extradition bill protests]]
**Hong Kong anti-extradition bill protesters briefly [[2019 Hong Kong anti-extradition bill protests#Storming of Legislative Council|break into]] the [[Legislative Council Complex]], which houses the [[Legislative Council of Hong Kong|local parliament]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/jul/01/hong-kong-protests-group-tries-to-storm-government-building (''The Guardian'')]
*[[LGBT rights in Japan]]
**[[Ibaraki Prefecture]] becomes the first in [[Japan]] to recognize [[same-sex partnerships]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2019/07/01/national/ibaraki-becomes-japans-first-prefecture-recognize-sex-couples/#.XRsgeXHgqUk (''Japan Today'')]
* [[David Hurley]] is sworn is as the 27th [[Governor-General of Australia]], succeeding [[Peter Cosgrove]]. [https://www.sbs.com.au/news/david-hurley-sworn-in-as-australia-s-governor-general (SBS News)]
